memory_update.text: DDOG should remain a reference anchor for the AI observability/security control-plane node, but it is high-attention and mega-cap, so it should not dominate underfollowed discovery.

VRNS is a promising underfollowed data-security and DSPM candidate for AI-readiness workflows; later layers must verify Copilot/RAG/AI-governance-driven demand rather than generic data-security renewals.
TENB maps to the exposure-management side of AI security; key validation is whether Tenable One and AI Security create measurable expansion into AI assets and cloud attack-surface prioritization.
PATH is a control-plane hypothesis for governed agentic automation; it requires strict falsification because legacy RPA deceleration could overpower the agentic-AI narrative.

Public-market coverage is thin for pure-play AI governance/data catalog vendors because several obvious assets are private or acquired; later passes should test adjacent public proxies in identity, secrets management, DSPM, API security, and GRC automation.

node: AI security, observability, data governance, and automation control-plane software
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the control-plane software node found one obvious reference anchor and three underfollowed candidates. The common chokepoint thesis is that production AI and agentic workflows increase the need for observability, data security posture, exposure management, governance, auditability, and workflow orchestration across hybrid cloud and regulated enterprise environments. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
